blocks.text: Mediation, Integration and Automation. This installed reference covers Studio, activities, tasks, groups, mapping functions, shared connections, runtime, deployment and Control Plane. It is available offline and contains no project data or credentials.

Activity fields are extracted from the Studio editor contracts. A shared field marked optional may still be needed for a selected mode or provider. Dynamic schemas are project-specific; the guide explains how Studio derives them rather than inventing their fields.
Use the tree or search to choose a topic. Activity pages have Configuration, Input, Output, Advanced and Errors tabs. Download the complete PDF for the same reference in a portable format.
Scope: this is a product reference, not a claim of provider certification or production security readiness. Read the Security section before shared or production deployment.

New projects open with a callable Subtask containing Start and End. Add a Starter Task for a configured event such as an HTTP listener or scheduler. Give each task a unique name. Studio replaces spaces in object names with hyphens. Start and End define the Subtask input and output boundaries. Call Sub Task selects a target and may resolve a dynamic override at runtime. Keep an explicit fallback when packaging must discover a called task.

Create activities on the canvas and connect transitions. Conditions use input, environment properties and earlier activity output. Validate Task and Validate Project before Run or Debug. Nested calls are shown in the debug process/activity tree.

Declare the task input using an inline schema or a project schema. Call Sub Task maps into that interface. Event starters receive data from their configured system; they do not require mapping an inbound event from a preceding activity. Real providers still require valid connection and listener configuration.

Map the End activity to the task output interface. A waiting Call Sub Task publishes the called result. Spawn without waiting does not provide the synchronous business result. Project-selected schemas determine actual child fields.

Run and ordinary Debug keep continuous starters ready for events until stopped. Activity Testing opens a paused session without starting event listeners. Debug stepping and breakpoints affect the active job; test-bench Run once executes only the selected activity, not a complete process.

Connect specific error paths or use Catch and Rethrow. Unhandled sub-task errors propagate to the caller. Missing task references, broken mappings, unavailable providers and malformed group graphs require correction before reliable execution.

Select an activity and open Input. Drag Data fields, Functions or Constants onto a target, or type an expression. The expanded input editor provides more space and applies edits only after Apply mappings. For typed suggestions enter a dot in a data expression, or press Ctrl+Space; Enter or Tab accepts a suggestion.

Use the Data tree for the actual saved reference names. A constant string is different from an expression; keep datatype conversion and quoting appropriate for the target. Structural schema nodes are populated through child fields; supported union/scalar targets accept whole values.

Repeating targets support For Each and For Each Group. Conditional mappings support If, When/Otherwise and Choose. String literals require matching single or double quotes; numeric and boolean literals are unquoted. Invalid mappings appear dark red. Enter validates the field, keeps focus on an invalid value, and advances to the next field after success. Conditions support parentheses, not, and, or, comparisons and function calls; quoted text is preserved. For example: (${input.amount} > 10 and contains(${input.status}, "ready")) or false.

Project functions use named parameters such as $value in their definitions, and custom:normalize(${input.name}) when called. Nested project functions work in Mapper, activity Input mappings, Map & Test and both Python archive formats. Calls must supply the declared argument count; missing definitions and excessive recursion produce errors. Built-in function pages list signatures and insertion templates, not guaranteed outputs for every input datatype.

JDBC named parameters such as :orderId create Input parameters.orderId after SQL analysis. Set the parameter datatype before mapping. SAP IDoc fields derive from fetched metadata; XML/JSON/flat data fields derive from the chosen schema. Call Sub Task fields derive from the selected task interface. Refresh metadata and validate after changing contracts.

Mapper uses the current selected project schema. JSON schema trees resolve local references and nullable scalar types; recursive structures are bounded. Runtime contract checks support local references, required fields, scalar types, enum/const, additional properties, allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not, array size and uniqueness, tuple items, string length, numeric bounds and multipleOf. Patterns and patternProperties use the bounded regex dependency. Common string formats, conditional contracts, property names, dependencies and contains counts are validated. Remote references and complete JSON Schema conformance remain outside the supported subset.

JSON Parse returns the parsed value directly. Duplicate-key policy supports First wins, Last wins or Error. JSON Render includes all mapped root fields and supports removing null properties. String constants use quotes; numbers, booleans and JSON object/array constants retain their types in Studio and both Python archive formats.

SFTP uses system or configured known-hosts files and verifies host keys by default. Private-key files, passphrases, SSH agent selection and connection timeouts are shared by Studio and Python archives. Explicitly disabling host-key verification permits unknown hosts.

pages.title: Transformation tests, templates and durable mediation

blocks.text: Map & Test includes independently saved input/expected-output cases, field differences, named lookup tables, immutable exported template versions, local version history and contract baseline comparisons. Template imports clear project-specific schema IDs. Both Python archives include run_tests.py and transform_jsonl.py; the latter transforms JSON Lines without executing connectors.

Use lookupTable(value, name, fallback), lookup(value, table, fallback), enrich(record, fields), joinBy(left, right, leftKey, rightKey) and chunks(records, size). Limits bound evaluation steps, execution duration and output size; workflow cancellation signals evaluation checkpoints. Input target search and collapse/expand controls help navigate large schemas.

General provides Deduplicate Message, Message Receipt, Replay Messages, Aggregate Messages and Split Records. Use the same explicit namespace and durable SQLite file for cooperating activities. Claims return fencing tokens; complete after successful work, fail on the error path and acknowledge the broker last. Replay lists failures or deliberately requeues one stable key. Purge removes expired completed records and retains failed/pending work.

Aggregation requires a stable message ID, a correlation/window key and expected count. Duplicate IDs do not increase the count; forward only when ready=true. A timed-out group needs explicit flush to emit partial records. Use a new correlation/window key for a new group. Local SQLite coordinates processes on one host; use persistent storage in containers. External side effects must be idempotent because these activities do not guarantee exactly-once external writes.

Payload limit is 1 MB, group limit is 64 MB and state capacity defaults to 256 MB. JSONL defaults to 16 MB per batch and 1 MB per output record. Pattern matching times out at 100 ms. These are bounded portable capabilities, not a distributed durable workflow engine or complete schema standards implementation.

AI Build accepts a requirement for the current Task or Complete Project. Review the design preview and generated definition before Apply. Generation alone does not deploy or run the application. Without a configured model key, the local blueprint builder is used.

Do not enter credentials or confidential payloads into AI prompts. The current prompt instruction to exclude credentials is not an enforced redaction boundary. Validate and test generated designs, and review the security report before enabling shared access.

Use the project tree to manage Tasks, schemas, resources and environment properties. The palette and searchable activity picker add activities to the canvas. Select and move activities, edit their display names, and configure transition conditions. Use Window for the XML/JSON viewers and comparison workspace.

Project export/import preserves editable design artifacts. Deployment export packages an executable application; these are different workflows. Installed samples open as editable project copies. Samples marked connection setup need your own provider configuration and credentials.
Themes include Plain Classic and Plain Studio with light/dark variants. Layout panes can be shown or hidden from menus. The status/footer area exposes background work and execution state.

blocks.text: On Windows, lazy persistent SSH transport workers bound native cryptography thread state. Every operation still opens and closes its own authenticated connection. MINA_SFTP_TRANSPORT_WORKERS defaults to 32 (1–128); set it before the first connection and restart after changes. At capacity, a new connection waits up to its configured timeout, then fails without closing another session. Host-key verification, algorithms, authentication and socket/subsystem timeouts remain enabled. Other operating systems use the normal transport. See the Windows SFTP memory verification guide.

Place HTTP Send Response on the same execution path as the listener or receiver. In Input, optional HTTPHeaders contains Content-Type, complex StatusLine and repeating Cookies. Map StatusLine.httpVersion, StatusLine.statusCode and StatusLine.reasonPhrase independently. Native HTTP/1 listeners send the mapped version (1.0 or 1.1) and custom reason phrase, including an empty phrase. HTTP/1.0 responses use Content-Length and close the connection. HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 require a matching negotiated version and no nonempty reason phrase; unsupported overrides fail before sending headers. HTTP/1 fallback on an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 listener does not support custom reason phrases. Unmapped fields use existing defaults, and existing full status-line strings still work. Mapped settings remain visible in statusLine execution output. DynamicHTTPHeaders contains repeating Headers with headerName and headerValue. Dynamic headers override standard/legacy headers; duplicate names remain separate header lines, including Set-Cookie. Legacy statusCode, contentType and headers mappings still work. If the endpoint declares a response schema, its fields are available for body mapping. An explicit Content-Type must be offered by the endpoint and acceptable to the caller.

blocks.text: Delivery, transactions and performance

Persistent sender workers are reused for the same resolved connection and execution scope. The cache is bounded; changing credentials/configuration frequently or exceeding the cache can create new workers. Native text messages and string application properties are the supported send path. Do not treat all editor choices as implemented native features. Retry after an ambiguous timeout can duplicate a message.
Implemented behavior and limitations

Important engine limitation: the one-shot receive bridge acknowledges client-mode delivery before closing, then the engine returns a local confirmation token. Confirm Message cannot undo that early provider acknowledgement. The direct Python listener uses a different persistent transport; do not transfer its guarantees to Studio/engine mode.

Troubleshooting procedure

Missing JAR/class/native bridge errors: check the installed driver directory, matching versions and packaged Java bridge. Authentication/destination failures: verify credentials, queue/topic permissions and the resolved environment destination. Timeout: inspect empty-receive results as well as faults. A successful send is not proof that another application consumed or processed the message.
Acceptance test

Acceptance: publish while Run is active, verify automatic flow start, stop during processing and check broker redelivery. Do not approve loss-sensitive processing until acknowledgement timing is verified.

blocks.text: Delivery, transactions and performance

Separate local enqueue, broker acknowledgement and downstream processing. Monitor background publisher errors and shutdown draining. Use stable business IDs and idempotent consumers when retries are possible. Producer reuse reduces warm-send overhead, but first connection, TLS, metadata and broker availability still affect latency; no fixed latency is guaranteed.
Implemented behavior and limitations

Runtime records live under messages[], not the editor top-level topic/partition fields. consumerCount is not implemented as a pool in the engine receive call. max.poll.records is forwarded as a native property and may be rejected by confluent-kafka. Manual commits can advance a partition past earlier records, so preserve processing/commit order. Do not claim this receive path is production-qualified without a provider test.

blocks.text: Delivery, transactions and performance

SAP transport success and business success are different. Inspect BAPI RETURN/status data even when the RFC call completes. Use bounded payloads and batches; parsing/rendering materializes documents in memory. Persistent outbound workers reduce JVM startup overhead but do not eliminate provider/network latency. Use a live Dynamic Connection session only within its owning runtime; never persist its ID for later reuse.
Implemented behavior and limitations

Close returns terminated/committed rather than connected. Sessions are process-local and expire after idle timeout; default is 600000 ms. A failed transactional worker call attempts rollback and removes its session. Ensure every branch closes its session. Do not confuse this with a JDBC transaction group or distributed transaction.

blocks.text: Delivery, transactions and performance

SAP transport success and business success are different. Inspect BAPI RETURN/status data even when the RFC call completes. Use bounded payloads and batches; parsing/rendering materializes documents in memory. Persistent outbound workers reduce JVM startup overhead but do not eliminate provider/network latency. Use a live Dynamic Connection session only within its owning runtime; never persist its ID for later reuse.
Implemented behavior and limitations

The adapter splits DATA.WA by the configured delimiter and returns strings. Embedded delimiters can split values incorrectly. SAP row-width/function restrictions still apply; rowCount=0 is potentially unbounded. A successful connection does not imply table authorization.

blocks.text: Troubleshooting procedure

SAP_CONNECTION: verify native-library loading, routing and logon credentials. SAP_RFC: inspect the function name, parameter metadata and SAP authorization/ABAP error. SAP_IDOC or SAP_SCHEMA: compare basic type, extension, release and saved field offsets with the actual payload. SAP_TRANSACTION: inspect TID/queue/context state before retrying. Some underlying paths raise generic runtime errors instead of the advertised editor fault code; retain the full message and trace.
Acceptance test
Acceptance: test a small known result, no matches, paging, authorization failure and values containing the delimiter.

blocks.text: Recent activity regression verification — 2026-11-17

The checked-out Mapper, Transformer, Data, Kafka, Pub/Sub and EMS/JMS changes were exercised with automated regression tests and complete flows. A JMS credential/default-factory inconsistency was found and fixed. This is a bounded regression qualification, not a guarantee of every provider, workload or deployment.
Verification matrix

Each flow below ran in **Run, Debug, Python direct archive and Python engine archive**. Archive tests generate and execute the archives. Run/Debug use the runtime and debug manager used by Studio; this verification did not include a fresh interactive browser session.

rows: Source/target validation and output auditing passed
Scripting-library transformation and schema-validated output passed
Nested streaming round-trip and byte/hash audit passed
Grouping, totals, uniqueness, XSD identity constraints and invalid-EOF output preservation passed
Actual isolated Apache Kafka 3.9.1 broker; publish/readback and exact-payload audit passed
Official local Pub/Sub emulator; publish/readback and payload audit passed
Actual isolated Artemis 2.40.0 broker, provider-default credentials; passed
Actual Artemis through the configured JMS factory, exercising the EMS activity path; passed

blocks.text: The full backend suite completed **747 tests: 736 passed, 11 skipped**, before the final JMS-only correction. The post-fix messaging subset completed **40 tests, all passed**, including the actual Java bridge authentication/reflection regressions and runtime credential-validation tests. The full suite covers mapping, transformation, XML/JSON/Data formats, nested repeats, archive execution and connector regressions beyond the fresh workload matrix. Skipped tests require external services or unavailable tools; they are not successful qualifications.

Studio contract tests now cover optional provider credentials and conditional JNDI settings for both JMS and EMS. The complete frontend script tests and production Studio build are rerun after documentation regeneration; results are recorded in the validation summary.
Fix and compatibility

When both JMS credentials are blank, the bridge now calls `createConnection()` so the provider can use factory defaults. Previously it always passed two empty strings. Explicit credentials still use `createConnection(username, password)` unchanged. Studio and Run/Debug no longer reject a provider-default configuration that direct archives could accept. JNDI requires naming/factory settings rather than an unused direct URL; naming credentials are optional unless the provider requires them. No broker authentication policy is weakened by this change.

Regression coverage checks missing/empty credentials, explicit username/password, a blank password, password-only and whitespace-username cases. Runtime tests also verify required JNDI fields and configuration preservation. Live tests use a newly compiled Java bridge. Rebuild the normal Studio/sidecar Java bridge and restart Studio to use the fix in an existing installation.

An initial temporary broker launch omitted its JAAS configuration argument. That test-harness setup issue was corrected separately; the retained final results use the properly configured broker. Earlier failed attempts are not counted as passing runs.
Limits and reproduction

Actual vendor EMS and hosted GCP were unavailable. Artemis proves the shared JMS/EMS activity code path, not EMS-provider compatibility or throughput. The Pub/Sub emulator does not prove cloud IAM, quotas, regional latency or service behavior. Kafka used a loopback single-node PLAINTEXT broker. TLS, failover, production security, vendor-specific settings and network topologies need their own qualification.

These fresh workloads do not repeat the prior 100,000-record/10-minute soak qualification and do not establish that memory leaks are impossible. Both Python archive formats were generated and executed on this Windows host with the required dependencies and provider drivers, rather than on a second clean machine. This work does not rebuild the Windows installer.

Use `scripts/kafka-local-qa.py`, `scripts/pubsub-emulator-qa.py`, `scripts/transform-stream-qa.py`, `scripts/data-stream-qa.py`, `scripts/data-group-qa.py` and `scripts/flow-throughput.py` for the corresponding tests. Use only dedicated temporary resources, matching Java/provider drivers, and a correctly configured local broker. The full backend command is `python -m unittest discover -s backend/tests -v` with the backend/dependency directories on `PYTHONPATH`. Studio checks are `node --test frontend/scripts/*.test.mjs` and `npm.cmd run build` in `frontend` after rebuilding help.

The sanitized machine-readable results are in `docs/validation/recent-activities-summary-2026-11-17.json`. Detailed local logs and generated test packages are under ignored `tmp/recent-*-20261117*`; they are test evidence, not deployable dependencies and do not need to be copied to another workspace.

pages.title: Mapper document operations and record enrichment

blocks.text: Mapper document operations and record enrichment

Mapper includes document and record functions for API updates, record matching, snapshot reconciliation, grouped summaries and explicit output masking. They use the same implementation in preview, Run, Debug, generic activity Input mappings and both Python archives. Source values are not modified by these functions.
Find and use the functions

Open **Input → Functions**. **Document** contains JSON Pointer/Patch/Merge Patch and change generation. **Collection** includes indexed joins, deduplication, `aggregateRecords` rollups and `reconcileRecords` snapshot comparison. **Privacy** contains explicit key redaction and text masking. Drag a function onto a target or type its name for suggestions, then supply the intended source and arguments. The Visual Mapper function library exposes the same entries.

rows: Select one exact JSON member or array item
Apply an ordered sequence of conditional updates
Merge objects, remove members with null and replace arrays/scalars
Generate a repeatable JSON Patch describing changes
Match records with composite keys using an index
Keep the first or last occurrence of each key
Calculate named count/sum/average/min/max values for composite-key groups
Separate inserted, updated, deleted and unchanged records between snapshots
Replace explicitly named fields throughout nested objects/arrays
Retain a chosen suffix and mask the preceding characters

blocks.text: Exact paths with JSON Pointer

Paths follow [RFC 6901](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc6901/). An empty pointer selects the document, `/` selects an object member whose name is empty, and `/rows/0/id` selects an array member. Encode `~` as `~0` and `/` inside a member name as `~1`. Dots are literal member-name characters, avoiding ambiguity between an object key containing a dot and a nested path. URI-fragment forms such as `#/customer/id` are accepted by `jsonPointer` too.

jsonPointer(${input.document}, "/customer/id")
jsonPointer(${input.document}, "/optional", "fallback")

A supplied default handles a missing member/index, not malformed pointer syntax. An existing JSON null remains null. Array indices cannot have leading zeros; the append marker `-` has no readable value.
Conditional document updates and generated changes

`jsonPatch` implements the `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy` and `test` operations defined by [RFC 6902](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc6902/). The function works on a private tree. A failed test, missing target or invalid operation fails the call without changing its source or returning a partial patch. Numeric equality treats 1 and 1.0 alike while distinguishing true from 1.
jsonPatch(${input.document}, ${input.patch})
Example operations:

Root add/replace/remove are supported. A remove with `"path":""` deletes the document. Inside that patch, a subsequent test, replace, copy/move from, nested add or second remove fails because the root no longer exists. A subsequent root add recreates the document. If it remains removed at the end, the function returns JSON null at MINA's value boundary. Mapper's **Null and missing values** policy then applies: the default omits the target field; **Preserve null / xsi:nil** retains null. This representation does not turn the absent root into an existing null during patch evaluation. Patch paths use pointer strings rather than URI fragments. Moving a value into its own descendant is rejected. Copying a subtree creates independent values.

`jsonMergePatch` follows [RFC 7396](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc7396/). Object members with null values are removed; nested objects merge; arrays and non-object patches replace the selected value. A root null patch returns null.

jsonMergePatch(${input.document}, ${input.changes})
jsonDiff(${input.before}, ${input.after})

`jsonDiff` produces deterministic operations with escaped pointer paths. It replaces changed arrays as a whole instead of attempting an expensive minimal edit sequence. Applying its result to `before` reconstructs `after`. An empty operation array means there is no change.

These are local document transformations. To send generated operations to an API, map them to the request body and choose the provider's supported content type, such as `application/json-patch+json` or `application/merge-patch+json`. The remote API must implement the corresponding update behavior; Mapper does not change it. These functions execute in native Mapper rules and generated XSLT bindings.
XSLT bindings for document functions

**Generate XSLT binding** detects the eight functions in source expressions and pipeline descriptors. It embeds their implementations in a self-contained **XSLT 3.0** stylesheet; no Python callback, extension function or external import is required. Bindings without these functions continue to use XSLT 2.0. Manual XSLT 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 bindings are accepted. MINA executes 2.0/3.0 with its isolated Saxon worker and includes the Saxon requirement in both Python archive formats. Generated bindings can be reopened as editable visual rules; hand-editing them continues to switch to manual binding mode.
JSON has maps, arrays and nulls that do not have a direct XML text-field type. For these functions, supply JSON document/record arguments as JSON text inside source XML elements. For example:

<input>
  <document>{"name":"Ada","password":"secret"}</document>
  <changes>[{"op":"remove","path":"/password"}]</changes>
</input>
jsonPointer(jsonPatch(${input.document}, ${input.changes}), "/name")

This generates a target XML text value `Ada`. Object/array/null results become JSON text in the target XML field, such as `{"name":"Ada"}` or `null`; strings, numbers and Booleans use scalar text. Choose a string-valued target XSD field for JSON document results. The functions do not invent an XML element schema from JSON keys. `maskText` takes ordinary source text. Literal JSON arguments, nested document calls and existing text pipeline functions can be combined. Source-path arguments in expressions, or `${...}` pipeline arguments, are evaluated dynamically.

The embedded functions also expose their palette names under `urn:mina:mapper:documents:1`. When authoring a manual binding from a generated one, use `md:jsonPatch($document, $operations)`, `md:joinRecords(...)`, etc. These return XDM values, so serialize maps/arrays explicitly when placing them in an XML text field. The generated binding handles this boundary automatically. The self-contained stylesheet is verified directly with Saxon 13, as well as through MINA; this is not a certification for every third-party XSLT processor. It uses XSLT 3.0 maps/arrays and JSON functions described by the [W3C recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xslt-30/). Numeric parsing uses Saxon's documented `number-parser` option to preserve large integer/decimal values rather than forcing JSON numbers through double precision; see the [Saxon JSON parsing options](https://www.saxonica.com/html/documentation13/functions/fn/json-doc.html). An external processor needs a compatible numeric parsing option to preserve that precision behavior.
Composite-key enrichment and reconciliation

joinRecords(${input.orders}, ${input.customers}, ["/customerId", "/region"], ["/id", "/region"], "left")
deduplicateRecords(${input.records}, ["/id", "/region"], "last")

`joinRecords` supports **inner**, **left**, **right**, **full**, **semi** and **anti** modes. Key arguments may be one pointer string or equal-length arrays of pointers. Comparisons are type-sensitive: strings and Booleans do not match numbers. Numerically equal integer/floating values match. Missing or null key components never match. Normalize text keys explicitly when case folding is needed.

Inner/left/right/full joins produce `{left: ..., right: ...}` envelopes, using null for an unmatched side. This preserves conflicting field names instead of silently overwriting them. Semi/anti joins return the selected left records. Repeated keys produce every matching pair. Left encounter order and right-match order are stable; unmatched right records follow in right encounter order.

The right side is indexed once. Joins still materialize their inputs and result; they are not constant-memory streaming joins. Choose batch sizes appropriate to your data and retain the documented output limits for high-cardinality matches.

Deduplication keeps first or last keyed records and preserves the encounter order of the retained occurrences. Records with missing/null key components are retained separately, preventing accidental deletion of incomplete data. No durable cross-run deduplication is implied; use the durable message-state activity for that purpose.
Grouped summaries for integration batches
Each group returns a record like:
{"key":["US","USD"],"count":3,"values":{"total":30,"average":15,"presentAmounts":2,"orders":3}}

Group order follows the first appearance of each key. Include currency, tenant or other business boundaries in the key to avoid combining unrelated amounts. Keys use one to sixteen JSON Pointers and must be present, non-null scalar values. String `"1"`, number `1` and Boolean `true` identify different groups. Duplicate keys are expected in a rollup. Input rows must be record objects.

Supply one to sixteen metrics with unique names (1–128 characters). `sum`, `average`, `min` and `max` require a `path`. Missing/null metric values are ignored. An all-missing group returns zero for `sum` and null for average/min/max. `count` without a path counts every row; with a path it counts non-null present values. Numeric text and Booleans are rejected by numeric metrics; normalize them explicitly before grouping. Unknown operations and misspelled metric configuration fields fail validation, including on an empty batch.

Numeric results are ordinary JSON numbers. Summation uses decimal arithmetic internally to avoid the usual `0.1 + 0.2` accumulation artifact; fractional results still have JSON/runtime numeric precision. This does not add a monetary rounding policy. Apply the business-required rounding explicitly. Numeric sum/average inputs are bounded to 1,000 significant digits.

Numeric minimum/maximum results also normalize integral values to JSON integers. Large numeric comparisons use lexical decimal values consistently with portable XSLT; for example JSON `1e30` and integer `1000000000000000000000000000000` do not produce a false snapshot update or JSON Diff merely because Python's binary float representation differs. This does not recover precision already lost by a caller before supplying a JSON number. Booleans remain distinct.
Reconcile source and target snapshots
reconcileRecords(${input.previous}, ${input.current}, ["/id", "/tenant"])
The result contains four arrays:
`inserted`: current records whose key did not exist previously.
`updated`: `{key:[...],before:{...},after:{...}}` records with the same key
but different values.
`deleted`: previous records whose key is absent from the current snapshot.
`unchanged`: current records equal to their previous version.

Inserted, updated and unchanged rows follow current-snapshot order; deleted rows follow previous-snapshot order. Object member order does not create an update; array order does. Boolean and numeric values compare differently, while numerically equal integer/floating key values match.

Keys must uniquely identify every row in each snapshot. Missing, null, non-scalar or duplicate keys cause an error instead of silently generating ambiguous changes. The whole function fails without modifying either input. An empty current snapshot classifies every previous row as deleted: supply complete snapshots, not an incomplete page or failed source fetch.

Map `jsonPointer(${last.changes}, "/inserted")` (or the corresponding result path) into downstream database, messaging or other activity inputs. These are change classifications only: the Mapper does not issue writes, retain durable CDC state, enforce transactions or guarantee delivery. Keep those responsibilities in the appropriate integration activities.

Both functions are available in the shared Input-tab drag/drop and suggestion palette, Visual Mapper pipelines/expressions, `mina::Records` script imports, preview, Run, Debug and both Python archives. Generated XSLT embeds standalone XSLT 3.0 implementations; downloaded bindings need no MINA callbacks. XML fields carry JSON text at that boundary. Inputs and results are bounded to 8 MiB, 100,000 rows per input array and the existing nesting/work limits. They materialize snapshots/groups rather than maintaining constant-memory streams. Result growth is checked while appending rows, including expanded before/after envelopes. For large datasets, partition by complete key groups/snapshots.
Reproduce the complete-flow and standalone XSLT checks with:
python -m unittest backend.tests.test_mapping_records backend.tests.test_mapper_document_xslt -v
See [record capability verification](validation/mapper-records-summary-2026-11-16.json) and [changed files](MAPPER_RECORDS_CHANGED_FILES.md).
Explicit masking of mapped output

redactKeys(${input.document}, ["password", "accessToken"])
maskText(${input.accountNumber}, 4, "*")

Key redaction matches whole field names case-insensitively at any depth, including records in arrays. The default replacement is `[REDACTED]`; a third argument can provide a different JSON value. It does not guess which fields contain sensitive data. Replacing a value can change its type, so verify the selected target schema.

Text masking retains four trailing characters by default. A suffix of zero masks the complete string; a suffix longer than the text exposes the whole short value. The marker must be one character. JSON null is preserved. This modifies mapped output; it is not encryption and does not remove source data from separately configured input/execution logs.
Script modules
Transformer scripts can import these same implementations:

%dw 2.0
import jsonMergePatch from mina::Documents
import redactKeys from mina::Privacy
output application/json
---
redactKeys(jsonMergePatch(payload, vars.changes), ["password"])

`mina::Documents` exports the four document functions, `mina::Records` exports joinRecords/deduplicateRecords/aggregateRecords/reconcileRecords, and `mina::Privacy` exports redactKeys/maskText. These are MINA extensions, not claims about another engine's standard modules.
Limits, errors and verification

Document arguments and results are restricted to JSON values with string object keys, finite numbers, depth at most 128 and serialized size at most 8 MiB. Native functions also enforce cumulative work limits (four million visited nodes and 128 MiB of serialized intermediate checks). XSLT checks each document against the depth/byte limits and four million nodes, and runs within MINA's existing isolated worker timeout, concurrency and 8 MiB XML input/output limits. It preflights join and redaction expansion before constructing the output. Additional limits are 10,000 patch operations, 100,000 input/result records, 16 key components, 8,192-character pointers, 1,024 redaction field names and 65,536-character masking inputs. Combined limits can reject a workload before an individual maximum is reached. Expanding joins and redaction replacements are checked before retaining oversized outputs. These limits are JSON-size/work guards, not an operating-system RSS quota.

An additional fix makes terminal End/HTTP Send Response mapping failures fail the task instead of being reported as successful completion. Generic Input function arguments now parse JSON arrays/objects consistently with Mapper expressions.

Tests cover all patch operations, pointer escapes/defaults, immutable sources, typed equality, diff round-trips, six join modes, deduplication, redaction/masking, limits, preview, generic Input mappings, failure propagation and both archives. The XSLT suite additionally covers all eight functions, generated-binding round-trips, standalone Saxon execution, manual bindings, target XSD validation, Unicode names/fragments, large integers, absent-root transitions and relative ZIP import execution. Invalid patches fail the task in all four execution modes.
The repeatable bulk benchmark is:
python scripts/mapper-standards-qa.py --records 100000 --output-dir tmp/mapper-standards-qa-new

This executes Start → one Mapper joining two record collections → End. Every joined row is audited; archive generation/startup/IPC and cleanup are included. It measures bulk collection processing rather than per-message orchestration, broker throughput or a long-duration soak. Actual interpreter RSS samples include fixture data, materialized results and runtime/logging overhead.
On 2026-11-16, each mode audited 100,000 unique joined records from two 100,000-record input collections:

The bulk operation is fast but materializes substantial data, especially with Debug snapshots and archive IPC. These measurements are not a constant-memory claim. See the [qualification report](validation/mapper-standards-summary-2026-11-16.json) and linked per-mode evidence for exact values.

pages.title: Nested Data records and large-file streaming

blocks.text: Nested Data records and large-file streaming

Parse Data and Render Data support nested column paths, repeating JSON-valued columns, byte-bounded file batches and recoverable malformed quoting. The same implementation is packaged for Run, Debug, direct Python and engine Python. Existing non-streaming activities keep their record/text outputs.
Nested objects and repeating children
Enable **Nested record structures** in Configuration. In Input, map:

Each CSV or fixed-width column keeps its declared name. Paths are JSON Pointers relative to one record. Parse creates the structure; Render selects the same paths. A JSON column can carry an object or arbitrary repeating children:

The `items` CSV cell contains JSON text for the entire `lines` array; ordinary CSV escaping preserves commas, quotes and newlines. Missing/overlapping paths fail in strict mode rather than replacing another mapped branch. Explicit array positions such as `/lines/0/sku` are also supported. Numeric segments create arrays; use a JSON-valued column for objects with numeric property names. Paths use `~1` for a slash and `~0` for a tilde in a member name. Without explicit overrides, dotted names such as `customer.id` become nested paths.

A selected XSD or JSON Schema can supply nested field names and types. A single repeating wrapper child is treated as the row collection; otherwise the root is the record. `recordElement` explicitly selects a repeating child when needed. Nested objects retain parent paths, and repeating fields become JSON-valued columns. This supports hierarchies **inside each logical row**. For related header/detail/trailer rows, enable explicit [record grouping and whole-file validation](DATA_GROUPS_VALIDATION.md); relationships are configured rather than guessed from unrelated rows.

Structured `records`/`Rows` output retains original JSON keys. The convenience XML view normalizes invalid XML names when no XSD is selected and rejects normalization collisions; use structured records for exact unusual JSON keys.
Parse a large file
Enable **Stream large files** in Parse Data. Map these Input fields:

rows: Source delimited or fixed-width file on the runtime machine
Destination UTF-8 JSON Lines file, one nested record per line
Optional UTF-8 rejected-record JSON Lines file
Source encoding; defaults to UTF-8 with BOM handling
Maximum records per batch; default 500, maximum 10,000
Raw/parsed record budget per batch; default 8 MiB, maximum 64 MiB
Raw/parsed record limit; default 1 MiB, configurable 256 bytes–64 MiB

blocks.text: The record limit must fit in the batch budget. A byte limit can end a batch before its row count. Stream mode processes the whole source and owns its cursor; manual `startRecord` and legacy `noOfRecords` are not used as stream offsets. Multi-character separators now use the bounded reader as well, so total file size is no longer limited to 64 MiB. Limits apply to records and batches.
The output is metadata:
{"streamed":true,"filePath":"/runtime/output/records.jsonl","recordCount":35000,"errorCount":0,"batchCount":350,"errorFile":null,"done":true}

The complete file is not returned as an array, XML document or text value. Unless XSD validation needs it, Parse does not build convenience XML for streamed batches. Intermediate records exist only within configured byte/count budgets.
Render a large file

Enable **Stream large files** in Render Data. Map `streamInputFile` to the Parse JSON Lines output and `streamOutputFile` to the formatted destination. JSON Lines input is UTF-8; map `formatOptions.fileEncoding` for the output encoding. Select the same nested paths/types and normal separators, widths and header settings.

Render emits the header once, preserves separators between batches, and honors the final-line-separator option. UTF-16 output has one encoding preamble because one writer owns the stream. The output is file/count metadata, not the entire formatted text. Malformed JSON Lines input fails atomically; it is not skipped silently. JSON column values reject duplicate names, non-finite numbers and excessive nesting.

Input/output/reject paths must differ, including aliases/hard links. Source files must remain unchanged while processing. Paths resolve on the executing runtime machine; use Input properties instead of embedding development-machine paths. Destination directories must exist. Files are staged alongside the destination, flushed and atomically replaced only after successful processing. Failures and cancellation remove partial files and retain the previous destination. There is no rollback after a completed replacement. Reject files are independently published before the main output; the pair is not a filesystem transaction.
Recover malformed quoted records
Enable **Continue on record errors** and choose `formatOptions.quoteRecovery`:
`bounded` (default) accepts valid multiline quoted fields. It buffers at most

`streamMaxRecordBytes` and `maxRecordLines` (default 1,000, maximum 10,000). When a quoted candidate is malformed, the first physical line is rejected and subsequent buffered lines are replayed as new candidates. Cursor checkpoints point to logical boundaries, so recovery also works across Parse batches.
`physical-line` treats each physical line as a record. Use this when the file
contract forbids multiline fields; broken quotes cannot absorb following rows.

With continuation disabled, malformed quoting still raises an activity fault. With continuation enabled, type/column/quote errors appear in `ErrorRows` or the stream reject file, and `errorCount` reports rejected records. Reject diagnostics are byte-bounded and may truncate raw text (`rawTruncated: true`). Invalid headers still fail because the field contract cannot safely be established.

An unclosed quote is inherently ambiguous: some later lines can look like a valid continuation. Recovery cannot establish business correctness or reconstruct missing characters. Choose physical-line mode for a single-line contract and review rejects and recovered records before accepting a feed. Rejected candidates are explicitly reported rather than hidden.
Validation and limits

Optional XSD validation remains available. The original validation checkboxes validate bounded batches. Enable **Validate complete file against XSD** for a disk-staged document and global keys/references/cardinality; this replaces batch checks for that stream. **Validate whole-file rules** adds counts, exact totals and disk-backed uniqueness. See the [grouping/validation guide](DATA_GROUPS_VALIDATION.md). Render validation happens before formatting; strict mode prevents truncation.

Nested paths/JSON records are bounded to 64 levels, layouts to 10,000 columns, explicit array indices to 1,000 and automatically allocated array slots to 10,000 per record. JSON-valued columns handle larger repeating child arrays within the byte/complexity limits. Fixed-width fields/fill cannot contain line breaks, which would corrupt physical record boundaries. String input and legacy record/text outputs remain available, but only file-stream mode avoids returning the entire result. Streamed writes do not provide message delivery guarantees or database transactions.
Verification

python -m unittest backend.tests.test_data_stream backend.tests.test_format_activities -v
python scripts/data-stream-qa.py --records 35000 --payload-chars 2048 --output-dir tmp/data-stream-new

On 2026-11-16, a 72,963,904-byte nested CSV file was parsed to JSON Lines and rendered back through complete Run, Debug and both Python archive flows. All 35,000 records were audited in each mode and output SHA-256 matched the source. Execution times were 4.72–5.44 seconds in this local run. Archive creation, startup/cleanup and audit passes are outside the timed interval. Sampled RSS growth was below 13 MB; 10 ms RSS sampling can miss short peaks and is not a constant-memory guarantee or long-duration soak.
See [verification results](validation/data-stream-summary-2026-11-16.json) and [changed files](DATA_STREAM_CHANGED_FILES.md).

pages.title: Header/detail/trailer groups and whole-file Data validation

blocks.text: Header/detail/trailer groups and whole-file Data validation

Streaming Parse Data and Render Data support explicit header/detail/trailer groups, per-group trailer controls and validation through end of file. The implementation is shared by Run, Debug, direct Python and engine Python.
Enable and map a grouped format
Enable **Stream large files** and **Group header/detail/trailer records** in Configuration. Map `formatOptions.recordLayouts` to a JSON object such as:

The base activity supplies delimiter, separator rule, line ending and encoding. Every role supplies its own fields/types and can override `fieldPaths`, widths, offsets, line length and fill. Role `fieldPaths` activates nested mappings for that role. With no explicit paths, **Nested record structures** enables dotted paths. Fields include the discriminator column: it is not silently removed.

Delimited matches select a zero-based column and a literal case-sensitive value before type conversion/trimming. Fixed-width matches use `{"start":0,"end":1,"value":"H"}` instead; `end` is excluded. A record must match exactly one role. The file contains role records, not a separate CSV column header; ordinary `header` settings do not consume the first role record.
Parse accepts this sequence:
Each completed group becomes one UTF-8 JSON Lines envelope:

{"header":{"kind":"H","orderId":"A"},"details":[{"kind":"D","sku":"A1","amount":"10.25","orderRef":"B"},{"kind":"D","sku":"A2","amount":"2.75","orderRef":"A"}],"trailer":{"kind":"T","count":2,"total":"13.00"}}

A new header requires the previous trailer. Details and trailers require an open header. EOF with an open group, unknown/ambiguous discriminators, and malformed control records fail the activity. Parse buffers one group rather than the complete file. Groups are bounded to 8 MiB/10,000 details by default; configured maxima are 64 MiB and 1,000,000 details. Each physical role record also obeys `streamMaxRecordBytes`. A single group must fit the selected limits; this mode does not split an oversized group or infer arbitrary recursive record grammars. Ordinary non-grouped streaming remains available.

Render consumes the same envelope format from `streamInputFile`. It writes header, details and trailer in order, checks each emitted discriminator, and honors encoding and final-line settings. Existing trailers are validated by default. Set `deriveTrailer: true` to create/recompute the configured fields; trailer `defaults` supply the marker and other static values. Unconfigured fields are not automatically invented.

Count checks compare accepted detail count. Sum checks use decimal arithmetic over the specified detail pointer. Values must be finite numeric strings or numbers; Booleans/missing values fail. Without `scale`, comparison is exact. With scale 0–12, the control is quantized using half-to-even rounding. Derived sums are decimal strings to preserve scale; count values are integers. Use string field types when the file must retain exact decimal lexical formatting. Overlapping/duplicate trailer control paths are rejected.
Whole-file rules
Enable **Validate whole-file rules** and map `formatOptions.wholeFileRules`:

{
  "minRecords": 8,
  "maxRecords": 8,
  "minGroups": 2,
  "maxGroups": 2,
  "minDetails": 4,
  "maxDetails": 4,
  "maxErrors": 0,
  "uniqueKeys": [["/header/orderId"]],
  "totals": [{"name":"amount","path":"/amount","expected":"13.30"}]
}

Count bounds are nonnegative integers. In grouped mode, records count accepted physical H/D/T records; groups count completed envelopes; details count accepted detail rows. `recordCount` in the activity result counts group envelopes, while `sourceRecordCount` reports physical role records. In ordinary streaming, records count accepted logical rows and group/detail counts are zero.

File totals apply to detail rows in grouped mode, or every row in ordinary mode. Each named total has a required pointer and expected decimal value. File totals are exact; normalize/round upstream if business rules require rounding.

Uniqueness applies to completed group envelopes or ordinary records. Supply up to 16 rules, each containing one to 16 composite JSON Pointer paths. Keys must exist, be non-null scalars and serialize to at most 64 KiB. Comparison is typed/case-sensitive; numerically equal integer/floating keys match, while Booleans and numeric strings remain distinct. A temporary disk-backed SQLite index avoids retaining all uniqueness values in a Python collection. It is removed on success, failure and cancellation.

Maximum limits fail as soon as exceeded; minimum limits and expected totals are checked at EOF. With rule validation enabled, `maxErrors` defaults to zero. Unknown settings, invalid bounds or missing total/key values fail explicitly. Whole-file rules also work without HDT grouping, across any batch size.
Complete-file XSD validation

Enable **Validate complete file against XSD**, select the project/inline XSD and select `recordElement` when the root has multiple repeating children. The XML contract is a root containing the repeating logical record/group element. Optional `wholeFileRules.rootAttributes` supplies required root attributes:
{"rootAttributes":{"batchId":"QA-2026"}}

The activity stages the complete logical XML document to disk, then validates through EOF using the packaged schema graph and a clearing incremental parser. Imports/includes follow the existing project-schema access restrictions. This checks root cardinality, facets and XSD identity/key-reference constraints across groups and batches. Forward references to a later group are allowed when the complete XSD permits them. Root attributes are not inferred as CSV columns.

Complete-file XSD validation replaces per-batch XSD checks for that stream, so a valid forward reference or whole-file minimum cannot fail merely because a batch ends early. The existing validation checkboxes retain batch semantics when complete-file validation is disabled. File rule validation and XSD validation are independently selectable.

The complete XML is disk-staged, not returned as a DOM or string. Standard XML depth/text limits still apply. XSD identity validation can retain key/reference state internally, so memory can grow with the number of identity values. Use disk-backed `uniqueKeys` rules where uniqueness alone is sufficient; there is no universal constant-RAM guarantee for arbitrary XSD constraints. Provision temporary disk space for staged output, XML and uniqueness indexes.
Failure, rejected records and publication

Every framing, trailer, file-rule and XSD check completes before the destination is atomically replaced. EOF failure preserves an existing output and removes staging files/indexes. This is atomic publication of one activity output, not a transaction spanning successive activities: a later Render failure does not roll back a previously successful Parse output. The reject file is independently published before the main output, as in ordinary streaming.

With **Continue on record errors**, bounded quote errors and conversion errors on recognized detail records may be rejected explicitly. Header/trailer type errors, unknown roles and invalid framing remain fatal because skipping them could change group ownership. Trailer controls still have to match accepted details. Whole-file `maxErrors` must explicitly permit rejected records; the default is zero. Recovery cannot reconstruct missing quotes reliably—use the physical-line policy for a single-line source contract and review diagnostics. Whole-file processing rejects Stop-at-blank-line mode so later records cannot escape validation.

Output metadata includes group/detail/source counts and `validation`, with `rulesValidated`, `xsdValidated`, final totals and the number of uniqueness rules. Keep stream paths property-driven on the runtime machine. Non-streaming activities cannot enable grouping or whole-file validation.
Verification

python -m unittest backend.tests.test_data_groups backend.tests.test_data_stream -v
python scripts/data-group-qa.py --groups 5000 --output-dir tmp/hdt-qa-new

On 2026-11-16, complete Parse → grouped JSON Lines → Render flows audited 5,000 groups, 10,000 details and 20,000 physical records per mode in Run, Debug, direct Python and engine Python. Every group was compared and rendered SHA-256 matched the source. A missing key reference at the end of each source failed the full XSD pass and preserved both pre-existing outputs. Execution took 5.61–5.82 seconds in this local synthetic run, excluding archive startup/cleanup and audit passes. These are functional/bulk checks, not a memory or long-duration soak benchmark.
See [verification report](validation/data-groups-summary-2026-11-16.json) and [changed files](DATA_GROUPS_CHANGED_FILES.md).

pages.title: Assisted mapping and automatic repeating structures

blocks.text: Assisted mapping and automatic repeating structures

Open a Mapper's **Input → AI Mapper**, then select **AI Map**. The assistant builds an executable mapping plan from schemas, contract metadata or JSON samples. It does not require an external AI account or send payloads to an external model. The confidence score is a local matching rank, not a probability of correctness.
Review, apply and undo
By default analysis leaves the current mappings unchanged. The review shows:
Suggested fields with source paths, confidence and matching reasons.
Automatically aligned nested repeating structures and repeated-value copies.
Protected existing mappings, ambiguous candidates and unmatched targets.
Required fields that still need attention.

Select **Choose this source** to resolve an ambiguous candidate, then analyze the updated choice. **Apply reviewed suggestions** applies the plan as one operation; **Discard plan** leaves mappings unchanged. **Undo AI Map** restores the mappings from immediately before application. Undo is disabled after a subsequent mapping edit so it cannot silently discard that edit. Existing **Require approval** may be turned off to apply safe suggestions directly after analysis.

Changes to schemas, samples, upstream contracts, mapping rules or analysis options cancel stale requests and discard the old review. An old response cannot replace newer edits. A manual stylesheet remains authoritative until the user selects **Use visual mappings** or **Use generated XSLT**; applying a visual plan is blocked while a manual stylesheet supplies the runtime output.
Detect repeating collections at every level
For example, a source can contain purchases with their own item collections:
{"purchases":[{"id":1,"items":[{"sku":"A","qty":2},{"sku":"B","qty":3}]}]}
For a target schema declaring `orders[].lines[]`, the Commerce vocabulary can produce this plan:

orders                    For Each last.purchases
  id                      last.purchases.id
  lines                   For Each last.purchases.items
    productCode           last.purchases.items.sku
    quantity              last.purchases.items.qty

The inner collection stays inside its own outer record. Independent collections are not flattened or combined into a Cartesian product. Repeating primitive values such as `tags: ["A", "B"]` use **Copy-Of**, preserving array values rather than creating empty objects. Generated XSLT supports these repeated scalar copies as well as ordinary complex collection loops.

Source and target repeating depths and shapes must agree for automatic matching. Repeating-to-scalar selection, aggregation and shape-changing coercions remain explicit mapping decisions. Turning off **Infer repeating structures** excludes automatic repeating mappings.
Source detection and vocabulary

The assistant uses the selected source schema first, then a supplied JSON sample. When neither is supplied, it can recover a schema from the single immediate predecessor's output contract. It preserves declared array cardinality instead of interpreting every child of a repeating parent as another array. Multiple incoming predecessors are not chosen automatically. For XML sample text, select a source XSD; a single XML example cannot establish the schema's cardinalities.
Open **AI mapping options** to choose a vocabulary:

Add project-specific source/target term pairs when domain names differ. These settings are saved with the Mapper. Case, camel case, underscores and hyphens are normalized for name comparison; generated paths preserve original spelling.

Matching checks data types, parent context and all repeating ancestors. Balanced matching uses names and hierarchy. Semantic matching gives more weight to business terms. Strict matching requires identical types; other strategies can accept integer-to-number widening. Exact matching uses normalized field names. String/number parsing, date reformatting and other transformations are not guessed.

Previously **Share reviewed mappings** pairs for the same schema structure can help suggestions. Sharing remains explicit and stores field-path preferences; the assistant does not automatically train on payload values. Reviewed alias paths are normalized so newly generated `last.*` mappings can be shared too.
Preserve existing work

Authored mappings, constants, disabled rules, conditions and duplicate occurrences are preserved. Ordinary active For-Each loops reading `last.*` can be reused to fill missing children when all schema ancestors agree; the existing loop and authored child rules remain unchanged. Grouped, conditional, duplicate and Copy-Of structures protect their descendants. A new loop is not inserted around authored child rules because that could change their execution scope. Clear or explicitly edit that structure to remap it. Blank direct placeholders can be filled; unapproved older suggestions are superseded by the new analysis. A protected field is not necessarily an enabled mapping, so required disabled targets are still reported for attention.
Navigate large maps

**Find field** filters source paths, existing mappings, target fields and review suggestions. **Unmapped targets only** includes disabled, unapproved and blank mappings; descendants already covered by an active Copy-Of are excluded. Rendering starts with 100 rows and **Show more** expands the view without removing mappings from the project or changing runtime behavior.

All rule target inputs share one autocomplete list. The editor no longer builds one full target dropdown per rule. **Add mapping** creates a blank rule at the top of the view rather than preselecting an unrelated source.
Validation and limits

Run **Run mapping test**, inspect Generated Output and resolve validation errors before saving. Required-field warnings are conservative schema guidance; conditional parent structures and provider-specific requirements still need testing. Suggestions do not prove business correctness or production readiness.

Analysis supports JSON Schema properties/local references, project-selected XSD structures (including resolved project dependencies), and JSON samples. Sample inference examines up to 32 records per array and merges observed optional fields. Empty/heterogeneous values cannot establish every type; select a schema for complete information. Wrap a root array in a named object field before automatic analysis. Format, enum and pattern constraints can require explicit functions and must still pass the mapping test. Names containing literal dots/brackets are not automatically mapped because the runtime's path notation would be ambiguous. Recursive or polymorphic schemas can require a narrower explicit structure/manual mapping.

Analysis is bounded to 64 levels, 20,000 visited schema/sample values, 5,000 fields per side and 5,000 final rules. It indexes exact names, vocabulary equivalents and tokens, limits candidates to 1,000 per field and one million comparisons overall, and asks for a narrower branch when these limits are reached. Conflicting loop alignments are left unmapped rather than mixing unrelated collections.

Verification covers nested/empty collections, repeated scalar copies, aliases, ambiguous choices, manual protection, required gaps, local references, XSDs, generated XSLT, Studio preview and schema-validated Run/Debug/both Python archives. Editor tests cover metadata inference and bounded, escaped review rendering.
On 2026-11-16 a synthetic 2,000-field plan took **0.070459 seconds**, examining 2,000 candidate pairs. Every mapped value was audited through complete flows:

columns: Elapsed seconds, including archive startup/cleanup where applicable

blocks.text: These are single bulk-field measurements, not UI interaction latency, message throughput or a long-duration memory soak. Reproduce with:
python scripts/mapper-assistant-qa.py --fields 2000 --output-dir tmp/assistant-qa-new
See the [verification report](validation/mapper-assistant-summary-2026-11-16.json) and [changed files](MAPPER_ASSISTANT_CHANGED_FILES.md).
Studio browser verification and saved-flow execution

The 2026-11-16 browser retest used the supported Chromium in-app browser with an isolated synthetic project. It exercised nested repeats, ambiguous matches, existing authored constants and loop reuse, Discard, Undo, manual source edits, sample edits, Save mapper and Input validation. Studio toolbar Run and Debug both delivered a scheduler event through Call Sub Task into the saved Mapper and completed the flow. Popup controls remained reachable at 1024 × 600 with 150% screen font as well as the normal 1280 × 720 view.

JSON samples now expose their nested object and array fields in the shared schema tree. Samples examine up to 32 records per array; select an explicit schema when later records may contain additional fields. Explicit JSON Schema and compact field definitions remain supported.

New assistant rules use `${last.field}` references, which are recognized in Input validation and source suggestions. Existing ordinary loops using bare `last.field` references remain supported. Preview preserves these aliases so old outer loops and new nested rules execute in the same scope.

Generated Output is cleared when mappings, test data, schemas or execution options change, including Undo. Run the mapping test again to see current output. An in-flight test is cancelled/ignored when its inputs change, and outdated saved preview values are removed from the configuration.

The browser-saved rules were executed unchanged through Run, Debug, direct Python and engine Python archives. Every output value was compared for the nested-repeat, explicitly chosen ambiguous source and existing authored-loop cases. The scheduler wrapper was also checked in Run and both archives; Studio drives its Debug event lifecycle interactively.
Recheck a captured QA project containing the `nested`, `ambiguous` and `existing` tasks with the same synthetic fixtures:

python scripts/mapper-studio-saved-qa.py --project tmp/saved-project.json --output-dir tmp/saved-mapper-qa-new
node --test frontend/scripts/mapper-assistant.test.mjs

These are functional checks, not a production throughput or long-duration soak claim. See [browser and execution evidence](validation/mapper-studio-ui-summary-2026-11-16.json) and the [files changed for this retest](MAPPER_STUDIO_UI_CHANGED_FILES.md).

pages.title: Transformation libraries, outputs, streaming and contracts

blocks.text: Transformation libraries, outputs, streaming and contracts

Mapper and Transformer share portable runtime support for these features in Run, Debug and both Python archive formats. Existing single-output projects retain their behavior. These additions extend MINA's embedded language; they do not install another vendor runtime or claim compatibility with every external script.
Reusable script libraries
In Transformer Configuration, expand **Reusable script libraries**. Add a module name such as `company::Names` and its declarations:

module Names
var prefix = "Customer: "
fun normalize(value) = upper(trim(value))
fun label(value) = prefix ++ normalize(value)
Import the module in any output script:

%dw 2.0
import company::Names as Names
output application/json
---
{name: Names::normalize(payload.name), label: Names::label(payload.name)}

Named imports (`import normalize from company::Names`) and wildcard imports are also supported. Library variables can be imported as constants. Declarations may span balanced parentheses, arrays or objects across lines. Functions have lexical module scope; they receive flow data through arguments. A module can import another configured module. Cycles, unknown exports and excessive import depth/work fail. Sources stay in the activity's `libraries` dictionary, are shared by its output scripts and travel with the project and both exports. No filesystem, network, Java or Python module loader is exposed through script imports.
Built-in module inventory:

rows: Explicit imports of existing core built-ins: upper/lower/trim, sizeOf/isEmpty, flatten, keysOf/valuesOf, sum/min/max/avg, joinBy/splitBy/contains/startsWith/endsWith, abs/floor/ceil/mod/pow, zip/unzip, uuid/now/typeOf/read/write
capitalize, camelize, underscore, dasherize, padLeft, padRight, substringBefore, substringAfter, reverse
fromBinary, fromHex, fromRadixNumber, toBinary, toHex, toRadixNumber
acos, asin, atan, cos, sin, tan, log10, logn, toDegrees, toRadians
joinRecords, deduplicateRecords, aggregateRecords (grouped metrics), reconcileRecords (snapshot change sets)

blocks.text: See [Mapper document operations](MAPPER_DOCUMENT_OPERATIONS.md) for standards, examples and limits for the MINA modules.

Only the listed overloads and the embedded expression syntax are supported; locale formatters, arbitrary custom types/namespaces and the complete external function libraries are not implied. `import` names outside the configured and built-in inventory produce a diagnostic. Library sources contain declarations; put a mapping body inside a function rather than an ignored module body.
Multiple output targets

Expand **Multiple output targets**, then choose **Add output target**. Each target has its own script and optional selected target schema. Supported targets are payload, attributes and a named variable. Only one payload and one attributes target are allowed; variable names must be distinct. Attribute results must be objects. Remove all output definitions to return to the original single target.

All scripts read the same original payload, attributes and variables. No target can observe another target's newly calculated value. The runtime calculates and validates every result before committing payload/attribute/variable updates. A script or contract failure leaves the previous attributes and variables intact. This transaction covers transformation state, not external service transactions. Subsequent activities can map `${attributes}` or `${attributes.field}` as well as the resulting payload and variables.

**Map & Test** displays every configured output and enforces the same contracts. Main single-output controls are disabled while multiple targets are active; edit each output's script, schema and visual mappings in its target section.
Visual/script synchronization

Expand **Visual / script mappings**. Static object fields appear as editable target-path/expression pairs, including nested fields and empty objects. Changing a field updates the script; script edits refresh this view after a short debounce. Existing headers, imports and declarations are retained on a visual edit.

An array, map/filter pipeline, conditional root or object that cannot safely be flattened appears as a whole-payload expression node. Editing that node updates the complete body without discarding it. Syntax outside the embedded parser's supported grammar reports an error and preserves the script. This view is an expression graph, not a promise to infer detailed field connections from arbitrary code. The existing Mapper visual/XSLT binding round-trip remains available for its documented mapping subset.
Source and target schema validation

Transformer source/target selections now enforce JSON Schema or XSD contracts in preview, Run, Debug and both archives. Validation is on by default when a schema is selected; explicit source/target checkboxes can disable it. Each additional output may select its own contract. XSD structure selectors choose the required root/type instead of validating against unrelated global structures.

Schema IDs reload the current project asset at execution, preserving the selected XSD structure. Project-relative XSD imports/includes and JSON Schema references resolve only from packaged project schema assets. Remote schema retrieval remains disabled. JSON types, required properties, formats and bounded patterns use the shared validator. XSD documents use the compiled project contract. XML-valued outputs validate as XML; structured outputs with XSD contracts are rendered against the selected structure for validation. Failures identify source or target and prevent output-state commit. Exports include the selected assets, transitive dependencies and deployment dependency declarations.
Record streaming for Mapper and Transformer

Expand **Streaming record transformation** in Mapper policies or Transformer configuration. Enable streaming, choose input/output formats and provide file paths. Paths can be dynamic expressions, for example `${input.sourceFile}` and `${properties.outputFile}`. Both paths refer to the machine running the flow; an exported application does not carry the user's input files.
Input formats: a top-level JSON array, JSON Lines or CSV (including quoted
multiline fields). JSON arrays use an incremental decoder, not a full-file load.
Output formats: JSON array, JSON Lines or CSV. Output is written one record at
a time. CSV columns come from the first output row; unexpected later columns fail rather than being silently discarded. The Python CSV parser's field-size limit also applies.
Mappings/scripts and selected schemas apply to one record. Whole-file sorting,
grouping and random access are not stream operations; apply them explicitly to each record or use a separate aggregation step.
Multiple Transformer targets write a per-record JSON/JSONL envelope containing
`payload`, `attributes` and `variables`. They do not accumulate file-sized arrays in flow variables. Multiple-target envelopes cannot use the CSV writer.
Run/Debug returns `streamed`, `recordsWritten`, `outputFile` and `outputFormat`;
it does not load the generated file into the activity result. Map & Test tests a sample record without opening the configured files.
Limits are configurable: maximum record bytes (256 bytes–8 MiB), maximum records
and a positive finite deadline. Defaults are 1 MiB, one million and 600 seconds. Invalid/incomplete JSON, duplicate CSV headers, oversized records, schema errors and cancellation fail the activity.
A sibling temporary output is flushed and atomically replaces the destination

only after the full stream succeeds. Failure or cancellation observed before commit removes the temporary file and preserves an existing destination. Cooperative cancellation drains the owned worker; a consumer never receives a half-written destination file.

This is file-backed, record-at-a-time streaming. It is not an in-memory stream object passed through every connector, nor an implementation of every external reader/writer property or nested-XML streaming convention. Memory scales with a record, its schema/module environment and fixed-size parser buffers, not the total record count. Full-record size guards apply before emission.
Verification

`backend/tests/test_transform_features.py` covers imports and lexical scope, transactional targets, preview parity, script round-trips, schema reloads/local references, XSD includes, streaming rollback/limits and all four execution modes. Generated archives are built and executed in independent Python interpreters.
The repeatable large-file qualification is:
python scripts/transform-stream-qa.py --records 100000 --output-dir tmp/stream-qa-new

It runs Start → streaming Mapper/Transformer → End for each execution mode, validates source and target schemas, audits every output, and samples the actual interpreter's RSS. Its timings include archive startup/import, readback and cleanup. Use a fresh output directory. These measurements are a bounded workload test, not a long-duration leak proof or a comparison against another product's runtime.
See the dated qualification summary and per-mode reports in `docs/validation/`.
On 2026-11-16, all eight 100,000-record cases passed with full readback and source/ target validation enabled:

Sampled interpreter RSS peaks were 37.89–70.45 MiB across these cases, including runtime/import overhead. The actual archive interpreter identifies itself to the harness; measurements do not accidentally sample only the Windows launcher. These samples alone do not establish long-duration memory stability.

The broad backend run completed 684 tests with 11 environment-dependent skips and no failures. A final 33-test focused run also passed after the property/ condition and cancellation refinements. See [qualification evidence](validation/transform-features-summary-2026-11-16.json).
Mapping and transformation qualification
Scope

The follow-up [runtime feature guide](TRANSFORM_RUNTIME_FEATURES.md) documents libraries, multiple targets, bounded file streaming, script synchronization and schema enforcement added after the initial measurements below. The original reports remain historical evidence; current feature qualification is separate.
MINA provides a schema-driven Mapper and a scripted Transformer. The tests use local migration fixtures and cover MINA behavior and performance.
XML namespaces and imports

New generated Mapper bindings declare the XPath function namespaces used by their expressions, including expressions inside Choose and Otherwise branches. Saved bindings reopen with their declared compatible function namespaces. Studio checks that the stylesheet still matches its editable mapping rules.

Project import identifies process extensions from the XML elements and attributes that use them. A conflicting process or an unreadable XML asset appears under **Review required** while other supported assets are imported. Namespace declarations are resolved locally.
Changes from this review
Equality no longer executes unrelated relational operators, and Boolean values
are distinguished from numbers in structured comparisons.
If/else, default, and logical operators skip evaluation of unneeded expressions
while still checking their syntax. Empty and null collections skip lambda execution; null-capable collection operations preserve null.
Object mapping supports value/key/index parameters, anonymous `$`/`$$`/`$$$`
parameters and dynamic object keys. `filterObject`, `minBy`, `maxBy`, `zip`, `unzip`, `mod` and `pow` are available. Mapper functions remain a separate palette.
Quoted Unicode text, subtraction without spaces, exponent-form numbers and
trailing whitespace work. Unknown identifiers/coercions and unsupported module imports, writer properties, language headers and output formats raise errors rather than silently changing behavior.
XML input retains attributes on leaf elements and handles MIME parameters.

The internal representation uses `@attribute` and `#text`; this is a MINA value representation, not an implementation of every XML selector in another language. XML output understands that representation. DTDs and external entities are disabled, parsing has normal tree limits, and XML input is capped at 8 MiB.
Repeated formulas reuse immutable token lists in a 128-entry cache. Payloads,
lambda environments and results are never cached. Expressions are capped at 64 KiB. This is token reuse, not compiled streaming execution.
Script execution runs off the async event loop in Run/Debug, matching the direct
archive's scheduling behavior. A regression verifies other async work can proceed.
The direct exporter accepts the Transformer's default operation, matching Run,

Debug and the engine archive. The pre-fix failed benchmark is retained as evidence. Both archives declare the XML reader's existing `lxml` dependency in their generated deployment checks, including scripts that select XML at runtime.
Studio includes object-filter and highest-score script starting points, with
updated activity help describing the embedded language subset.
Capability assessment

rows: Selected XSD roots/types, inline contracts, occurrence markers and source views
Source/target schema selection for script generation
Not a claim of identical designer controls; script schema selection is not full source/output validation
Copy-Of, For-Each, grouping, If/Choose and independent duplicate occurrences
Objects/arrays, conditions, defaults and collection lambdas
Existing Mapper regressions plus new scripted semantic cases
General functions, XPath 1.0/2.0 catalogs, custom functions and lookup tables
Configured module imports, constants, multiline functions and listed built-in modules
Not all proprietary extensions or every external library/overload
Offline XSLT 1.0/2.0, generated binding round-trips within the documented subset
Not full namespace-aware script selectors, mixed content, writer settings or proprietary parallel XSLT extensions
Use schema mapping with Parse/Render activities
JSON, XML, CSV and plain text paths
Not every binary, Java object, spreadsheet, copybook or flat-file format supported by other engines
Schema validation, source coercions and occurrence overrides
JSON Schema/XSD source and target enforcement with packaged local references
